items.note: Subjective experience is often treated as the core of phenomenal consciousness.
The words are often used interchangeably, but awareness is sometimes kept distinct.
One concerns experience and the other performance. Their relationship is debated.
Basic sentience is among the senses of creature consciousness.
Researchers ask how consciousness relates to attention and information processing.
Whether consciousness-related notions apply to artificial systems is disputed.
Intelligence is often analysed as a feature of cognition.
Machine intelligence is defined through behavioural tests or formal measures.
Performing intelligently is not obviously the same as understanding.
Understanding is commonly analysed as grasping meaning.
Whether artificial systems understand is the central dispute in the Chinese Room literature.
Memory is one kind of cognitive process.
Psychological-continuity views of personal identity rest on memory.
Awareness is studied alongside attention and other cognitive functions.
AI uses 'agent' for systems that act toward goals.
Formal definitions of machine intelligence are built on agents.
Sentience is the capacity for felt experience.
Capacity to feel and capacity to perform are different.
Awareness and experience are close but not identical concepts.
Whether language models have access to meaning is disputed.
